title: Telegram capability absences — preconditions, not losses
why: Four rows that record what is *not* there in the Telegram channel: no native command menu (`set_my_commands` returns zero hits while 45 CommandHandlers exist), no `/help` for anyone but admins (only `help_admin`), no `ConversationHandler` anywhere, and no client conversational AI. They carry no capability because the capability is missing, and the sweep deliberately kept them rather than dropping them — an absence that is written down cannot be rediscovered as a surprise. But they are not inert bookkeeping: `S-451` and `S-452` are sequencing preconditions for the Telegram reply-keyboard retirements recorded in the rows above them; `S-453` records that all multi-step flow state lives in the bot process and does not survive a restart; and `S-454`'s note states plainly that **CHAT IS THE PRIMARY MAYA OS USER INTERFACE is currently FALSE for clients in this channel** — a client who writes to the bot is handed off to the app, and every client-facing disposition above is contingent on a producer existing. None of the four is a primary-nav entry, so none is part of the primary-navigation collapse; their weight is as conditions on decisions recorded elsewhere.
disappear: Nothing in this group — all four rows are absences, and the retirement condition on three of them is `NOT RETIRED — it becomes a capability`. That is true of O06 read alone: the retirements this group gates sit in the neighbouring Telegram reply-keyboard rows, and if O06 is left unresolved those retirements take discoverability and the second route to help with them. `S-451` carries the sweep's default class line (`MOVE INTO CHAT WIDGET`, `RETIRE AFTER PARITY — K16`), but the row itself says nothing exists to lose; read it as a gap to fill, not as a retirement.
remain: The absences, recorded — and each row already names its own successor from evidence, so this is not a group where "nothing is replaced": an in-conversation capability index for `S-451`, role-aware help reachable by any phrasing for `S-452`, durable multi-step flow state for `S-453`, client conversation with Maya for `S-454`. What actually requires the owner's signature is the canonical owner on all four rows — the inventory row names no capability. K8 (`S-451`) and K8/K10/K11 (the other three) decide whether each is filled, and `S-451`'s note fixes the order. Until `S-453` is filled, multi-step Telegram flows stay in-process only — module-level dicts on a manual 30-minute TTL, dropped by a bot restart — while the app-chat mirror is already durable. Today the only such flow still in use is the owner's own broadcast, and it reports the loss rather than swallowing it, so the cost of leaving `S-453` unfilled is in the stateful flows a chat-first Telegram would add, not in what breaks now.
risk: LOW as attribution — signing the owner name on four recorded absences retires nothing and removes no check. What is not low sits in the neighbouring rows, and the order matters: `S-451`'s own note calls the inverse risk severe and requires the in-conversation capability index to ship BEFORE the reply keyboards are retired, not after; `S-452` records that retiring the master keyboard leaves ten exact normalised phrases as the sole route to help for every non-owner, admins aside. `S-454` keeps the programme's foundational claim false for clients in this channel until a producer exists. Approve O06; do not approve the neighbouring reply-keyboard retirements until `S-451` and `S-452` are filled.
user_impact: Approving O06 by itself changes nothing any user can see: all four rows are recorded absences in the native Telegram bot, not surfaces being moved or removed. Two of the four describe conditions already live. A client who writes to the Telegram bot gets the app-handoff line instead of a conversation with Maya (S-454) — verified at bot.py L86-92 (`_get_ai_response_async` returns `client_handoff_message(APP_URL)`), the terminal handoff in `process_message` at L2775-2776, and `handle_contact` at L2409-2412. S-453 is real but narrower than the row's example set: of the four module-level flow dicts (L103-126) only `broadcast_flow` is still written, and only behind `canonical_staff_access.is_admin` (L2143-2146, L2195-2197, L3564-3566). `booking_flow` and `gift_cert_flow` have no assignment anywhere in bot.py, `_finalize_booking` (L2844-2846) is a handoff stub, `_finalize_gift_cert` always takes the "сертификат не выбран" branch, and `_handle_digital_cert_input` (L2914) has no caller — so no client can lose a half-composed booking or gift-certificate flow, and masters have no multi-step flow at all; the exposure is the owner's broadcast flow alone. Nor is the loss silent: a flow missing at confirm time answers "Превью устарело — запусти /broadcast заново" (L2029-2031). The sharper defect this row points at is not restart-dependent — the "✏️ Свой текст" branch sets stage `awaiting_text` and asks for the text as the next message (L2142-2150), but `process_message` (L2727-2776) has no consumer for that stage: `_admin_busy_in_flow` (L2544-2547) suppresses admin NLU and the owner's typed broadcast falls through to the client handoff line, dropped on every attempt, restart or not. The user-visible risk from the other two rows lands later and only if sequencing is wrong: there is no native "/" command menu (no `set_my_commands` call anywhere in the package, S-451) and no `CommandHandler("help")` — only `help_admin` at L5030 (S-452) — so if the Telegram reply keyboards retire before an in-conversation capability index and free-phrasing help exist, a master's only remaining route to help is typing one of the ten exact phrases in `_COMMANDS_REQUEST_PHRASES` (L2696-2701), matched by strict set membership after normalisation (L2703-2708). Admins keep `/help_admin` and the admin NLU "help" intent; masters and clients do not.
security_impact: NONE for authority — approving this group removes no check of any kind, because nothing is being retired here; it records four things that are already missing. Direction note: the S-454 absence is fail-closed and deliberate, not a hole. The docstring at bot.py L91 is "R01: raw native Telegram carries no canonical Client channel proof", and the same refusal is applied consistently — `handle_contact` (L2409-2412), `_finalize_booking` (L2844-2846), and the `is_retired_client_callback` gate in `handle_callback` (L1703-1705) — i.e. client conversation is refused in a channel with no canonical Client identity and handed off to the verified app, so restoring client chat here in K8/K10/K11 is the step that would need a server-side identity proof, and O06 is not that step. One over-claim must be withdrawn: it is not true that no role decision is made in this channel. `canonical_staff_access.is_admin(chat_id)` and `master_projection(chat_id)` decide staff role inside the bot process, keyed on the raw Telegram chat_id that R01 itself calls non-canonical, and that decision gates a full-base broadcast and free-text admin actions. This is a pre-existing property of the channel, neither created nor removed by O06 and not what these four rows evidence — but it should be stated, not described away. The S-453 weakness is availability, not authority, and for a tighter reason than "no reconstructable trail": an interrupted flow produced no effect to reconstruct, and every authority check is re-evaluated at the point of effect (`broadcast_send` re-checks `is_admin` at L2025-2027, as do the `bcast_custom` and `bcast_tpl_` branches at L2143-2145 and L2195-2197), so lost flow state fails closed rather than open. Nothing here touches the frozen limitations: no enforcement is asserted (Gate 10 remains measured, not enforced), no STEP_UP channel is implied, admin gating is role-gating and explicitly not separation of duties, and no claim rests on attendance confirmation while GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM is open.
